title: CBT skills path
description: Six short lessons for self-guided practice. This is not a clinical treatment program.

lessons.title: Map a pattern
points: A situation, your interpretation, your feelings, your body responses and your actions can affect one another.
Mapping one moment can show where a small change might be possible. It is a working description, not a diagnosis.
practice: Write what happened, what went through your mind, what you felt or noticed in your body, what you did, and what happened next.

lessons.title: Choose a workable goal
points: Pick one current difficulty you can influence.
Make the first step specific and small enough to try. A realistic plan is more useful than an ambitious plan you cannot start.
practice: Describe what you would like to do differently.
Name one first step, when you could take it, and what might get in the way.

lessons.title: Plan an activity
points: When your routine gets smaller, you may have fewer chances for enjoyment, achievement or connection.
A manageable activity can be a useful experiment. Notice how it goes rather than expecting it to fix your mood.
practice: Choose one activity and a time for it.
Make it small enough to do. Afterwards, note what you did and what you noticed.

lessons.title: Examine a thought
points: A thought can feel like a fact, especially when an emotion is strong. It may still be one interpretation of what happened.
The aim is a fair, useful view that includes the evidence—not forced positivity.
practice: Write down one thought linked to a strong feeling.
Note what supports it, what does not support it, and a more balanced way to describe the situation.
Compare the feeling before and after. Either result is useful information.

lessons.title: Test a prediction
points: A prediction is something you expect will happen. A small, safe experiment can help you learn whether it happens as expected.
Choose an experiment that is respectful and low risk. Do not use it to test medical advice, physical safety or another person’s private information.
practice: Write the prediction in a way you could observe.
Choose one small action that could give you information.
Afterward, record what happened and what you would conclude now.

lessons.title: Solve a problem and keep what helps
points: For a practical problem, define one part you can act on, list possible options, choose a workable one and plan its first step.
For uncertainty you cannot solve, choose how you want to respond while it remains uncertain.
Review which skills helped, what made them hard to use, and who you could turn to for support.
practice: Write one problem in a single sentence.
List two possible next steps and choose one to try.
Name one sign that the problem is returning and one response you could use.
